Reference / locale/case

locale/case#

Text in the case a language writes it.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

LocalizedCase(text: "istanbul", locale: Locale("tr")).upper();      // "İSTANBUL"
LocalizedCase(text: "DİYARBAKIR", locale: Locale("tr")).lower();    // "diyarbakır"
LocalizedCase(text: "iğdır ılıca", locale: Locale("tr")).title();   // "İğdır Ilıca"
LocalizedCase(text: "ÌR", locale: Locale("lt")).lower();            // "i̇̀r"

Description#

Text in the case a language writes it. Turkish and Azeri pair the dotted and dotless i (I and ı, İ and i); Lithuanian keeps the dot above i and j when an accent stands over them, and drops it again in capitals. Every other language takes the Unicode default case mapping, as string.lower() and upper() do. The rules are Unicode's SpecialCasing.txt.

title() starts each word with its title case and lowers the rest (Unicode's toTitlecase): "ǆemal" is "ǅemal", "ßa" is "Ssa", and Georgian keeps its letters. A word is a run of letters, marks, digits and connectors such as "_", joined across an apostrophe, a full stop, a colon or a middle dot that stands between two of them, so "don't" is one word and "3rd" begins with its digit. Anything outside a word keeps its title case on its own.

The Greek final sigma follows string.lower(): "ΟΔΟΣ" is "οδος".

object LocalizedCase

A text and the language whose case rules apply to it.
